headline: Carney courts China on trade as US auto tariffs squeeze Canada
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday and agreed to further tariff cuts as Ottawa seeks alternatives to US-bound auto exports. Facing thousands of auto job losses from American tariffs, Canada recently opened a low-tariff quota for 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles, angering Washington.
why_it_matters: Because 90% of Canadian-made cars are sold in the US, Ottawa’s pivot toward Chinese EVs signals a major rupture in North American trade.
source_search: Carney courts China on trade as US auto tariffs squeeze Canada BBC

headline: Nvidia forms board national security panel after CEO scandal
summary: Nvidia on Tuesday established a board-level National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson, days after CEO Jensen Huang resigned over an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Existing security and trade compliance teams will report to the quarterly panel ahead of earnings.
why_it_matters: Tighter governance aims to reassure investors and Washington after a 28% monthly share slump eroded hundreds of billions in value from the AI chip leader.
source_search: Nvidia forms board national security panel after CEO scandal DW

headline: US curbs Chinese remote AI chip access ahead of APEC summit
summary: The US Commerce Department issued an interim rule curbing Chinese firms from remotely accessing advanced AI chips through foreign data centres. Exporters now need licenses to ship advanced semiconductors to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil. Beijing condemned the curbs as economic coercion disrupting global supply chains.
why_it_matters: Closing cloud computing loopholes forces Southeast Asian data centre operators into stricter compliance and heightens US-China trade tensions just days before high-stakes presidential talks.
source_search: US curbs Chinese remote AI chip access ahead of APEC summit Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Britain sanctions Israeli builders over West Bank settlement expansion
summary: Britain on Tuesday imposed asset freezes and director bans on eight Israeli property and construction firms accused of building West Bank settlements, alongside activist group Tzav 9 for blocking Gaza aid convoys. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband warned that projects like the 1,200-home E1 plan endanger a two-state solution.
why_it_matters: Targeting corporate developers directly marks a sharper financial escalation by a longtime Israeli ally to deter settlement construction around eastern Jerusalem.
source_search: Britain sanctions Israeli builders over West Bank settlement expansion The Hindu

headline: Waymo halts US freeway robotaxi rides after California DMV ban
summary: California's Department of Motor Vehicles banned Waymo robotaxis from state freeways after autonomous vehicles entered an active Highway 101 construction zone near Burlingame and encountered patrol cars on Highway 280. Although issued November 11, the order emerged Tuesday. Waymo halted freeway rides across all 15 US operating cities.
why_it_matters: Losing highway access forces Waymo onto slower surface streets, eroding the faster airport and cross-metro travel times central to scaling commercial robotaxi services.
source_search: Waymo halts US freeway robotaxi rides after California DMV ban TechCrunch

headline: BJP sets Hindutva and Mathura temple pitch for Uttar Pradesh
summary: BJP leaders concluded a two-day strategy meeting in Mathura on Tuesday, deciding to make a grand Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi temple a central Uttar Pradesh poll issue. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya outlined the pitch as the party prepared to label Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav anti-Hindu.
why_it_matters: Reviewing every sitting legislator while elevating the disputed Mathura temple issue shows the BJP is countering anti-incumbency and worker discontent ahead of UP polls.
source_search: BJP sets Hindutva and Mathura temple pitch for Uttar Pradesh Indian Express

headline: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion to push AI drugs into trials
summary: Isomorphic Labs raised $5 billion on Tuesday in a Series C round co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital. Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz, and Thrive Capital joined the Google DeepMind spinoff six months after its $2.1 billion round. The capital will move oncology and immunology drugs toward clinical trials.
why_it_matters: Raising over $7 billion in six months signals enormous investor confidence that computational biology can shorten timelines and cut costs in pharmaceutical development.
source_search: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion to push AI drugs into trials Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Tiger Woods schedules December golf comeback after two-year absence
summary: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf in December at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas, his first appearance since the 2024 Open Championship. Woods, 50, took an exemption into the 20-player PGA Tour-sanctioned event after injuries, a five-year driving ban, and treatment following a March arrest.
why_it_matters: Returning in a 20-player event without FedEx Cup points lets Woods test his recovery in competition while signalling whether golf's biggest draw can resume full play.
source_search: Tiger Woods schedules December golf comeback after two-year absence BBC Sport

headline: Supreme Court rebukes MP Sanjay Raut over remarks targeting judiciary
summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday rebuked Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut during criminal contempt proceedings over social media posts targeting Chief Justice Surya Kant and the judiciary. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi asked Raut to file another affidavit after his counsel conceded the remarks were indefensible.
why_it_matters: Demanding a fresh affidavit after an incomplete apology signals the court's strict boundary against elected lawmakers attacking judicial institutions on social media.
source_search: Supreme Court rebukes MP Sanjay Raut over remarks targeting judiciary The Hindu

headline: Iran strikes Bahrain radar base and denies US dirty-bomb report
summary: Iranian Revolutionary Guard drones targeted a US-operated radar at Bahrain’s Sheikh Isa Air Base on Tuesday, marking the third attack on the Gulf state in five days. Tehran also dismissed a CNN report alleging an Iranian dirty-bomb plot against US officials, after President Donald Trump threatened severe retaliation.
why_it_matters: Renewed strikes on Bahrain after a lull since September risk undermining regional mediation by Qatar and Oman as rhetoric between Tehran and Washington sharpens.
source_search: Iran strikes Bahrain radar base and denies US dirty-bomb report The Hindu

headline: Apple blames internal update after global iCloud and Pay outage
summary: A widespread outage hit Apple Pay, iCloud, App Store, and Apple Music globally from 9:51 PM IST on November 17. Users reported sudden sign-outs and failed iPhone activations. Apple blamed an internal update, not a cyberattack, days after Microsoft Outlook and Teams went offline for 30 hours.
why_it_matters: Back-to-back disruptions at Apple and Microsoft expose the fragility of global digital infrastructure and heighten pressure on enterprises to adopt multi-vendor cloud redundancy.
source_search: Apple blames internal update after global iCloud and Pay outage Inc42

headline: Plaid Cymru's first Welsh budget boosts NHS but squeezes departments
summary: Welsh Finance Minister Elin Jones unveiled Plaid Cymru's first £30 billion budget Tuesday, adding £500 million for the NHS and £176 million for councils while trimming four other departments. Without a Senedd majority, the government reserved nearly £150 million to negotiate opposition support ahead of February's decisive vote.
why_it_matters: Passing the budget in February will test Plaid Cymru's minority administration as below-average health funding increases and departmental cuts force tough political trade-offs across Welsh public services.
source_search: Plaid Cymru's first Welsh budget boosts NHS but squeezes departments BBC

headline: Foreign inflows lift Nifty Bank to record high of 62,273
summary: The Nifty Bank index reached a record 62,273.5 on Tuesday as foreign institutional investors bought Indian lenders. Twelve of fourteen index stocks gained, led by Punjab National Bank jumping 3.74 percent to ₹150. November inflows and 20 percent Q2-FY27 earnings growth helped reverse two years of sector underperformance.
why_it_matters: Financials account for up to 40 percent of foreign investors' Indian exposure, meaning sustained overseas buying could anchor broader domestic equity market gains.
source_search: Foreign inflows lift Nifty Bank to record high of 62,273 Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour after LIV Golf collapse
summary: Two-time US Open champion Bryson DeChambeau has joined the DP World Tour for next season as LIV Golf winds down after losing Saudi funding in April. Granted category one status, the 33-year-old American receives full European Tour entry and a top-10 pathway back to the PGA Tour.
why_it_matters: Landing one of LIV Golf's biggest draws strengthens the DP World Tour's star power while reshaping men's professional golf as former breakaway stars return to traditional tours.
source_search: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour after LIV Golf collapse BBC Sport

headline: SAG-AFTRA drops thousands over unpaid dues amid leadership pay backlash
summary: SAG-AFTRA terminated thousands of members on November 1 for falling 18 months behind on dues, ending a six-year pandemic-era pause. The removals follow a board vote extending executive director Duncan Crabtree-Ireland's contract by four years with a 15% raise on his $1.1 million salary, fueling internal discontent.
why_it_matters: Expelling struggling performers during a severe production downturn risks fracturing the actors' union and undermining member solidarity over future contracts, healthcare security, and AI protections.
source_search: SAG-AFTRA drops thousands over unpaid dues amid leadership pay backlash Variety

headline: US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991
summary: Global health authorities announced Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, formally recognising the disease as endemic after 26 years. The reversal follows the worst US outbreak since 1991, with over 5,400 cases and eight deaths reported in 2026 under Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr.
why_it_matters: Returning to endemic transmission means a preventable childhood virus now circulates continuously in the United States, raising hospitalization risks and straining public health defences.
source_search: US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991 The Guardian

headline: Kerala High Court dismisses lawyer’s contempt plea against district judge
summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday dismissed lawyer T.B. Mini’s petition seeking contempt action against District Judge Honey M. Varghese over alleged remarks in the 2017 actor assault case. Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan ruled the plea relied solely on hearsay, while affirming that lawyers deserve fair treatment from the Bench.
why_it_matters: The ruling shields trial judges from hearsay-based contempt petitions while warning both courts and media against amplifying disputes that damage legal institutions.
source_search: Kerala High Court dismisses lawyer’s contempt plea against district judge The Hindu

headline: Over 146,000 march across France demanding public-sector pay rises
summary: At least 146,000 protesters marched across France on Tuesday, including 28,000 in Paris, as public-sector workers and students demanded higher pay to offset rising living costs. Unions launched the third nationwide strike since September after failed talks with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu over a frozen salary scale.
why_it_matters: With France’s 5.8 million public employees losing 16% purchasing power since 2017, sustained strikes complicate the government’s push to pass a cost-cutting budget.
source_search: Over 146,000 march across France demanding public-sector pay rises Al Jazeera

headline: Google extends retention of temporary Gemini chats to two months
summary: Google is extending how long it stores temporary Gemini chats and history-off conversations from 72 hours to two months globally. The company cited safety, security, and system recovery, adding temporary chats will not train models. Google also separated chat history from AI training controls into distinct user settings.
why_it_matters: Retaining temporary chats twice as long as OpenAI or Anthropic sharpens the trade-off between AI abuse monitoring and users' expectations for private, ephemeral conversations.
source_search: Google extends retention of temporary Gemini chats to two months TechCrunch

headline: Congress refuses below 100 UP seats as SP balks at 181
summary: Congress leaders led by Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi met in Delhi on Monday to prepare for Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, insisting the party will not contest fewer than 100 of 403 seats. The stance follows ally Samajwadi Party refusing Congress’s initial demand for 181 constituencies.
why_it_matters: Clashes over traditional strongholds like Amethi and Rae Bareli could strain INDIA bloc unity before joint campaign plans begin in December.
source_search: Congress refuses below 100 UP seats as SP balks at 181 Indian Express

headline: SEBI slashes commodity derivative margins to lower domestic hedging costs
summary: SEBI cut initial margins on agri and non-agri commodity derivatives effective December 1, 2026. Margins drop to 2 percent from 6 to 8 percent on lower volatility contracts, and to 3 percent from 10 percent on highly volatile commodities, reducing electronic hedging costs for one year.
why_it_matters: Cheaper margin collateral lowers capital requirements for farmers, processors, and traders, encouraging deeper liquidity and wider price discovery across India's commodity exchanges.
source_search: SEBI slashes commodity derivative margins to lower domestic hedging costs Hindu BusinessLine

headline: England's Jacob Bethell to miss South Africa Tests after knee setback
summary: England batter Jacob Bethell will miss the Test tour of South Africa after suffering a training setback in Australia that requires a second right-knee surgery. The 23-year-old, sidelined since July, was also released by IPL side Royal Challengers Bengaluru over fitness doubts for the 2027 season.
why_it_matters: Losing a promising top-order batter who struck an Ashes century in January forces England to reshuffle its Test batting lineup before a demanding winter and home Ashes series.
source_search: England's Jacob Bethell to miss South Africa Tests after knee setback BBC Sport

headline: Netflix drama 'The Body' opens with 5.1 million streaming views
summary: Quinn Shephard's teen psychological drama 'The Body' debuted at number three on Netflix's November 9–16 TV chart, drawing 5.1 million views within five days of its November 11 premiere. Only second-week titles 'Taken: Natalee Holloway' at 7.2 million and 'Black Doves' Season 2 at 6.6 million ranked higher.
why_it_matters: Strong five-day viewership positions a new original teen drama as an immediate podium contender alongside established Netflix franchises and true-crime docuseries.
source_search: Netflix drama 'The Body' opens with 5.1 million streaming views Variety

headline: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth
summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft reached one light-day from Earth on November 18, crossing roughly 26 billion kilometers after 49 years and two months in flight. Launched in 1977 and traveling at 61,000 km/h, the probe is the first human-made object at that distance and still transmits interstellar data.
why_it_matters: Signals now take two full days for a round trip to NASA, demonstrating the engineering endurance of a probe still returning unprecedented deep-space measurements.
source_search: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth DW

headline: Government keeps Palantir on £330m NHS data contract until 2029
summary: Ministers will keep Palantir running England's £330 million NHS data contract until 2029 instead of triggering an early exit next year. Despite opposition from MPs and the British Medical Association over data use and Palantir's defence ties, procurement for British replacement suppliers will only begin next summer.
why_it_matters: Delaying a switch until 2029 prolongs NHS reliance on a controversial US contractor while exposing tensions between operational continuity in reducing hospital backlogs and domestic data sovereignty.
source_search: Government keeps Palantir on £330m NHS data contract until 2029 BBC
